newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Under pressure from weak gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Under pressure from weak gasoline.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices are under pressure this week from weak gasoline, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Free-on-board Singapore MTBE prices were flat at around $255-$260 per tonne, a shade lower from last week's assessments of $255-$265.
"There is a lot of downside pressure," a trader said. "Demand here is not much -- either for (gasoline) blending or for the mandated markets, and the U.S. gasoline market is not fantastic."
Gasoline demand in Thailand and Taiwan -- where the use of MTBE in petrol is mandatory -- was lacklustre.
Thai refiner Bangchak will only issue its regular import tender early next week for its July requirements, a company official said.
Meanwhile, weak regional buying interest for high octane gasoline was in turn dampening demand for the gasoline octane enhancer.
"Only CPC (Taiwan) is looking for 95-octane gasoline. The rest of the buyers like India and Indonesia only require low RON material," a trader said.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a tender to buy its third July arrival 95-octane unleaded reformate cargo, a company official said.
The official said the tender, which seeks 250,000-barrels of unleaded reformate for July 24-August 15 delivery to Keelung, Kaohsiung, Shalung or Taichung, closes June 17 and is valid for two days.
"In the last tender, the award price was not so good," the official said. "We needed two cargoes, so now we are looking for more."
Traders also expected U.S. support to diminish as gasoline prices weaken there.
"NYMEX gasoline is taking a tumble ... the question is whether U.S. MTBE can hold," a trader said.

API data showed a bigger than expected build in gasoline which could start to weigh on the market in coming weeks. The build halved a year-on-year deficit and is gradually erasing support for the gasoline price.
